cues.text: Text classification means: read a text, give it one label.
This email: spam or not spam? This review: positive or negative?
We will look at three classic ways to decide.
First, Naive Bayes. It asks: how often does each word appear in each class?
Good appears mostly in positive reviews. Bad appears mostly in negative ones.
Every word gives its vote, and the class with the highest score wins.
It is called naive because it treats every word as independent of the others.
Second, logistic regression. Every word gets a weight.
Good adds to the score. Bad takes away from it.
Then the sigmoid squashes the score into a probability between zero and one.
Above one half, we say positive. Despite its name, it is a classifier.
Third, the support vector machine.
Picture the positive and negative reviews as points.
The SVM draws the line with the widest empty gap between the two groups. That gap is the margin.
Its score tells the side of the line. It is not a probability.
For the exam:
Naive Bayes counts words per class. It is fast and a strong baseline.
Logistic regression gives a probability.
SVM finds the widest margin.
In a project: start with Naive Bayes, then try the others.
